chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام that he said:

A man from the people of Khurāsān said to him: “O son of the Messenger of Allah, I saw the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in a dream, as though he was saying to me: ‘How will you be when a part of me is buried in your land, you are entrusted with my trust, and my star is concealed in your soil?’”

So al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to him: “I am the one buried in your land, and I am a part of your Prophet, and I am the trust and the star. Indeed, whoever visits me while knowing what Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has made obligatory of my right and my obedience, then I and my forefathers are his intercessors on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever we are intercessors for shall be saved, even if upon him were the like of the burden of the two weighty beings, the jinn and humankind. And indeed, my father narrated to me from my grandfather from his father عليه السلام that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘Whoever sees me in his sleep has indeed seen me, for Shayṭān does not assume my form, nor the form of any of my awṣiyāʾ, nor the form of any one of their Shīʿah. Truly, the truthful vision is one part from seventy parts of prophethood.’”

key_terms.أَوْصِيَائِي: my successors; the designated successors of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الرُّؤْيَا الصَّادِقَةَ: the truthful vision; a dream that is true and veridical
key_terms.الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection and final reckoning
key_terms.بَضْعَتِي: a part of me; referring to close essential connection with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.شُفَعَاؤُهُ: his intercessors; those who intercede on his behalf on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.شِيعَتِهِمْ: their Shīʿah; the followers devoted to the awṣiyāʾ
key_terms.نَجْمِي: my star; a mark of guidance and distinction
key_terms.وَدِيعَتِي: my trust; that which has been entrusted for safekeeping

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Riḍā’s hadith say about visiting him, intercession, and seeing the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله in a dream?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام as the one intended in the dream seen by the man of Khurāsān, describing his burial there as the burial of a part of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. It emphasizes the Imam’s right, obedience, and intercession on the Day of Resurrection, and also affirms that a true dream of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله is genuine because Shayṭān cannot take his form or the form of his awṣiyāʾ.
